title: Traffic-conditioned probe mixer and multi-signal rollback oracle
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds traffic-conditioned probe scheduling and a multi-signal rollback oracle that fuses latency, throughput, and error signals to reduce false positives in canary rollouts. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via canary config.
description:
Motivation: existing canary probes run at fixed rates across slices which can over- or under-probe under heterogeneous traffic. This causes noisy regression alerts and either wasted probe budget or blind spots during production rollouts. This PR introduces a traffic-conditioned probe mixer (TCM) that adaptively allocates probe budget to traffic cohorts using a lightweight stochastic scheduler, and a multi-signal rollback oracle (MSRO) that fuses latency percentiles, throughput deltas, and error-rate trends with a de-glitching stage to avoid spurious rollbacks.

What this changes: single-line summary: add TCM scheduling service, probe weighting heuristics, MSRO fusion engine, metrics adapters, unit+integration tests, and docs/runbook.

Details: the TCM observes per-route traffic histograms (shape, concurrency, recent QPS) and produces a probe mix vector per-cohort. The mixer uses a softmax-weighted reservoir sampler that favors under-observed slices and high-variance slices. The probe sampler is shape-aware: short-paths receive higher frequency but smaller batch probes; long-paths get fewer but deeper probes that exercise KV cache and long-context kernels. The MSRO ingests three signal streams: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput delta (relative to baseline), and error-rate trend. Signals are normalized by rolling robust statistics (median-of-means for variance estimation) then fed into a small logistic fusion model with an explicit deglitch stage: short transients (under configured half-life) are suppressed unless corroborated across two signals or persisted across two probe windows.

Deglitch algorithm: median-of-means on sliding windows + Bayesian change-point detector tuned for low false alarm rate. When a potential regression is detected, MSRO computes a composite risk score (0.0-1.0). Score > 0.85 triggers immediate canary pause + automated narrow rollback; 0.6-0.85 opens an investigation ticket and reduces canary weight by configurable fraction. Configs are exposed in canary.yaml under spec.probes.mixer and spec.probes.rollback.

Backward compatibility & rollout: TCM/MSRO are opt-in on canary resources. Default behavior unchanged. We provide a migration guide and example canary manifests in docs/runbooks/perf-canary-tcm.md.

Testing and validation: unit tests for mixer heuristics and deglitch logic; integration tests that run synthetic traffic shapes (stepped, bursted, long-tail) against a canary controller in a local kind cluster. Also added a replay-based regression test that replays a known noisy incident trace; MSRO reduces false-positive alerts by ~72% in the replay compared to the legacy detector (benchmarks in docs/benchmarks/tcm-replay.md).

Operational concerns: added observability hooks: per-cohort probe allocation metrics, composite risk_score metric (tagged by canary_id), and a debug endpoint to fetch current probe mix. Default probe budget limits are conservative to avoid additional load.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and runbook added - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Backwards-compatible opt-in config - [x] Benchmarks and replay artifacts - [x] CI green (rerun after flaky test fix)

Related work: builds on ENG-2146 (probe reservoir refactor) and ENG-2210 (canary telemetry harmonization). Incident SUP-4321 motivated the deglitch thresholds and replay harness.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the deglitch thresholds (pkg/canary/deglitch.go) and the mixer fairness heuristics (pkg/canary/mixer.go). The fusion model is intentionally lightweight (no external dependencies) to keep the canary controller footprint small.

Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/TCM-MSRO-design, replay artifacts: docs/benchmarks/tcm-replay.md
